- When sentiment is consistently negative (0.00 or low) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 2–5% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85.00), model often overshoots and forecasts too high for next 3–5 days — cap forecast at 5–10% below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive (1.00) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop — adjust downward by 1–3% of recent range or use sentiment-weighted mean reversion.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term mean reversion (e.g., 30d forecast peaks too early) — delay peak forecast by 1–3 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.50–0.67), model tends to average out — use sentiment-weighted median or apply 10% smoothing to avoid overfitting to recent volatility.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a 30d forecast peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–7 days — especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
